what_it_is.prose: Rafael is one of Israel's largest state-owned defence OEMs and a long-standing Indian partner across missile systems. Its Indian footprint includes: the Spike ATGM family (a $500M deal announced 2017 was initially scrapped Nov 2017 but Spike-LR ATGMs were later acquired by the Indian Army via emergency procurement in Dec 2019; Spike-NLOS delivered to the IAF in Aug 2023); co-development with IAI/DRDO of the Barak-8 (LR-SAM/MR-SAM) family; the Iron Dome interceptor (Tamir missile) where Rafael is in talks (2026) to set up Indian production to meet export and Israeli demand; and the Kalyani Rafael Advanced Systems (KRAS) joint venture in Hyderabad — India's first private missile subsystem manufacturing facility. KRAS has secured orders including a $100M order for 1000 Barak missile kits.

faq.question: Did India buy Spike anti-tank missiles from Rafael?
faq.answer: India's relationship with the Spike ATGM has been stop-start. A $500M contract for Spike was announced in March 2017 but cancelled in November 2017 in favour of DRDO's Nag MPATGM. After Nag trials underperformed, the Indian Army acquired Spike-LR via emergency procurement in December 2019, and the IAF took delivery of Spike-NLOS in August 2023 for helicopter-launched long-range strike.

faq.question: What is KRAS in the Indian defence context?
faq.answer: KRAS — Kalyani Rafael Advanced Systems Pvt Ltd — is a Hyderabad-based joint venture between Kalyani Group (Bharat Forge) and Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, established around 2017. It is India's first private missile subsystem manufacturing facility and has secured orders such as a $100M contract for 1000 Barak missile kits, plus supplies for the Barak-8 programme.

faq.question: Is Iron Dome going to be made in India?
faq.answer: Rafael was reported in July 2026 to be in talks to set up Tamir interceptor (Iron Dome) production in India, primarily to meet Israeli domestic demand and export orders — leveraging Indian manufacturing capacity. This would be a Make-in-India arrangement rather than an Indian procurement of Iron Dome batteries.
